name: Spherical Dimension
definition: For a finite binary class $\mathcal H$, let $\Delta_{\mathcal H}$ be its space of realizable distributions on labeled examples and let $\Delta_{\mathcal H}^{\mathrm{ant}}=\Delta_{\mathcal H}\cap(-\Delta_{\mathcal H})$, where $-$ flips labels. The **spherical dimension** $\mathrm{sd}(\mathcal H)$ is the largest $d$ for which there is a continuous antipodality-preserving map $S^d\to\Delta_{\mathcal H}^{\mathrm{ant}}$.
graph_summary: Largest sphere that maps continuously and antipodally into the class’s label-flip-symmetric realizable-distribution space.
description: Finite-class version only; the distinct finitely supported, simplicial, and infinitely supported variants are intentionally not catalogued here.
origin_references: Introduced by Chornomaz, Moran, and Waknine in \cite{chornomaz2025spherical}.

monotonic.proof: Proposition 27 of \cite{chornomaz2025spherical} proves monotonicity for the class preorder, which includes deleting hypotheses.

p_monotonic.proof: Proposition 27 of \cite{chornomaz2025spherical} proves monotonicity for the class preorder, which includes restricting the domain.

doubly_monotonic.proof: The cited preorder monotonicity covers both subfamilies and projections.

c_monotonic.proof: Conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection, so it follows from double monotonicity.
